title: Graphic Development and Its Relations to Verbal Language in the French ELFE Nationwide Birth Cohort
abstract: ABSTRACT This study investigated the association between graphic and language skills in 5329 children (2651 girls and 2678 boys) from the French Elfe birth cohort, considering the influence of environmental factors. At 3.5 years, children completed the Draw‐a‐person test and parental reports at 2 years provided data on language production (lexical and syntactic levels), sociodemographics and activities. Sex‐stratified zero‐inflated Poisson regression models, controlling for child sex and family socioeconomic status, were utilized for analysis. The results showed that greater language skills (estimated through MacArthur–Bates Communicative Development Inventory language score—continuous or in quartiles—and making two‐word sentences at age 2) were associated with a lower likelihood of a null drawing score in both boys (OR = 0.89, 95% CI = 0.86; 0.93) and girls (OR = 0.88, 95% CI = 0.83; 0.93). Additionally, higher language skills correlated with a higher drawing score, but this was only significant in girls ( β = 0.01, 95% CI = 0; 0.02). In conclusion, higher language skills are linked to a greater probability of completing the Draw‐a‐person test for both sexes, while the relationship between language skill and drawing complexity was specific to girls in this cohort.
